findings.title: Anonymous auth now blocks on synchronous DB write
findings.body: Authenticate() previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with its own timeout and never blocked login. It now calls anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously on the request context, which when device_limit is enabled does a COUNT plus an INSERT/UPDATE on every anonymous request. This adds DB latency to the hot auth path and makes anonymous logins fail/slow when the DB is slow, and request cancellation aborts the tag. The tagging should stay async or use a detached context with timeout, with only the limit-reached case enforced synchronously if needed.

findings.title: Device limit check has TOCTOU race, limit can be bypassed
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice() does CountDevices() then, if count < limit, falls through to an unconditional upsert INSERT ... ON CONFLICT. Two concurrent requests for two new devices can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the limit. There is no unique-count enforcement in the DB, transaction, or advisory lock. Under burst anonymous traffic the configured limit is not actually enforced.

findings.title: Any zero-row update is reported as device-limit-reached
findings.body: updateDevice() returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected == 0. That conflates 'new device, limit reached' (intended) with 'device row is older than 30 days so outside the BETWEEN window', 'row was just deleted by cleanup', or transient zero-row cases. In particular a stale device returning after 30d of inactivity (row still present until the 61d cleanup) can never refresh once the limit is reached, and a legit insert that lost a race is misreported. Callers in client.go treat this error as fatal auth failure, so misclassification locks users out.

findings.title: Provider signature change breaks DI and testability
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService() changed its injected dependency from anonStore anonstore.AnonStore to sqlStore db.DB and now constructs the store internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. This breaks any existing wire caller/test that supplied a custom AnonStore (e.g. mocks/fakes), removes the ability to decorate the store, and hides the limit wiring inside the constructor. Keep accepting AnonStore (or both) and wire ProvideAnonDBStore separately so DI graph and tests remain stable.

findings.title: AnonymousDeviceLimit serializes 0 instead of omitting unlimited
findings.body: FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit is int64 without omitempty, so the unlimited default (0) is sent as 0 while the TypeScript config declares anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined. Frontend code cannot distinguish 'unlimited' from 'limit of 0', risking a UI that thinks no devices are allowed. Use *int64 with omitempty or omit zero, matching other optional frontend settings.
